05. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. This interlocutory application has been filed by the Petitioner-Appellant seeking his release on bail.
3.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner-Appellant, at the outset, submitted that initially the Petitioner faced charges for commission of offence under Section 376(AB) of I.P.C. read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner-Appellant further submitted that in the meantime the Petitioner has faced trial and he has been convicted for commission of offence under Section 354-A of I.P.C. read with Section 10 of the POCSO Act and he has been sentenced to undergo R.I. of 5 years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/-, in default, to undergo R.I. for further period of three months for the aforesaid offences.
In the present appeal, the judgment dated 10th July, 2023 convicting the Petitioner-Appellant in the aforesaid sections has been assailed.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner-Appellant further submitted that the Petitioner has been languishing in custody since 01.03.2022, i.e. for more than 3  years, although he has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years.
On such ground, learned counsel for the Petitioner-Appellant submitted that the Petitioner be released on bail on any stringent terms and conditions otherwise the appeal may be infructuous.

sentences.text: On perusal of the record, it appears that notice issued to the Informant has been duly served on the Informant.
However, no one appears on behalf of the Informant.

5. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the release of the Petitioner-Appellant on bail on the ground that allegation made against the present Petitioner-Appellant is grave and serious in nature.

He further submitted that the Petitioner-Appellant has already been suffered the conviction for commission of offence under Section 354-A of I.P.C. read with Section 10 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years.
He further contended that the Appellant-Petitioner has failed to make out any ground for his release on bail.

6. On careful consideration of the submissions made by the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on analysis of the materials on record and further keeping in view the fact that Petitioner-Appellant has been convicted for a period of 5 years, out of which, he has already undergone sentence for more than 3 years, this Court observes that there is no possibility of early hearing of the matter.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that unless the Petitioner-Appellant is released on bail, the appeal preferred by the present Petitioner-Appellant might infructuous.
7. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner-Appellant on bail.

8. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner-Appellant be released on bail by the learned Additional Sessions Judge- cum-Presiding Officer, Special Court under POCSO Act, Mayurbhanj, Baripada in C.T. Case No.19 of 2022 on such terms and conditions as it may deem just and proper.
It is made clear that violation of any of the conditions, which is likely to be imposed by the trial court, shall entail cancellation of bail.
9. The I.A. is disposed of.

10. Heard.
11.

Realization of fine amount under the impugned judgment in C.T. Case No.19 of 2022 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Presiding Officer, Special Court under POCSO Act,
Mayurbhanj, Baripada, shall remain stayed till disposal of the appeal.
12. The I.A. is disposed of.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.

( Aditya Kumar Mohapatra) Judge Debasis Tarasankar Sahu @ Tulu vs State Of Odisha on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163414005/
